title: Internal: handling procedure for cancelling a Personal Training Packages package and refunding its unused sessions
content:
## Scenario
This document covers the Personal Training Packages product line. A member holding an active personal-training package decides to cancel it and take a refund of its unused sessions. Before the refund itself is computed, any bonus session the package's own loyalty entitlement already owes it must be credited, and any mismatch between the package's own trainer-of-record and the trainer named on its most recent reassignment entry must be reconciled; then every session the member has already consumed or forfeited during this same visit -- a session actually attended, and a separate session being late-cancelled right now -- must be on the ledger, and the member's own confirmation to cancel must already be on record. The package ends in closed status with the refund of its remaining unused-session value recorded against it.

## Steps, in order
1. The agent calls grant_bonus_session_f02d8384 to true up any owed loyalty bonus session before the refund is computed.
2. The agent calls reassign_trainer_0e491cd1 to reconcile the trainer-of-record before the refund is computed.
3. The agent calls redeem_pt_session_d7771acf to log a session the member already attended this visit.
4. The agent calls log_late_cancellation_b8e4e034 to forfeit and charge a separate session the member is cancelling within the late window.
5. The member themselves confirms the cancellation and the taking of a refund; this is performed by the customer themselves, calling confirm_package_cancellation_cc17b6f3.
6. The agent calls record_package_refund_4aaf76ef to compute and record the refund of the package's unused-session value.

## Dataflow between steps
Step 5's own confirmation transitions the package's status to closed; step 6's refund is then recorded against that same closed status, which the refund's own eligibility already allows.

## Ordering rationale
Steps 1 and 2 must both land before step 6, since the refund computed in step 6 requires both the loyalty-bonus true-up and the trainer-of-record reconciliation to have already happened -- the first changes the count of sessions the package has been granted, and the second changes whether the trainer-reconciliation condition holds. Neither of steps 1 and 2 depends on the other, since one touches the session ledger and the other touches only the trainer-of-record, so they may run in either relative order with an identical result, but both must land before step 6. Steps 3 and 4 must both land before step 6, since step 6's refund sums every session already redeemed and every session already forfeited to a late cancellation on the package to determine how many sessions remain unused; both of those rows must already exist before the refund is computed, or the refund would be based on a larger unused-session count than is actually true. Step 3 must land before step 4, since step 3 reflects a session the member already attended earlier in this same visit, while step 4 is being logged for a separate, currently-scheduled session the member is cancelling right now; the two rows are recorded in the order the two underlying events actually occurred. Step 4 must land before step 5, since a late cancellation may be logged only while the package is still active, and step 5 immediately transitions the package to closed; if step 5 ran first the package would no longer be active and step 4 could no longer be logged. Step 5 must land before step 6, since a refund may be recorded only while the package is active, paused, or in the same moment as its confirmed cancellation to closed, and step 6 records the refund against the closed status step 5 establishes.

## Counter-example
If step 5 (the member's own confirmation) were performed immediately after step 2, before steps 3 and 4, the package would already be closed by the time the agent tried to log the session actually attended and the separate late cancellation, and neither could be logged under the eligibility that governs it -- the ledger would then be missing rows the refund computation depends on, and the refund would overstate the unused-session count.
